content:
In June this year, we noted three cases where apps belonging to clients of a US-sanctioned Russian bank bypassed App Store review to appear on the store. Two months later, another example has reached the top of the iPhone App Store.

"K8CHEN PRO" is the latest case. The App Store listing is disguised as an augmented reality (AR)-driven kitchen design app.

Upon opening, the app quickly "tears off" the disguise. The app's privacy policy link, hosted on the App Store, is stated to be auto-generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — which in itself may be a red flag.

Regardless, the app is undoubtedly a client application of T-Bank. What I find interesting is how these applications are able to repeatedly pass through App Store review.

Once they get enough exposure and climb high in the App Store rankings, it becomes obvious that these are not applications that should be there. The situation is quite puzzling.

The other cases mentioned in June can be found here and here.

Update: Sure enough, the app has been removed from the App Store.
